patent: Parallel link robot with delta-type legs, assigned to Fanuc Ltd; priority 2009-10-26, filed 2010-07-16, issued 2012-11-13. The patent names no product. Problem: adding rotational axes to a delta. The two prior-art routes each cost something: a telescoping center shaft from a base-mounted motor (FIG. 12) limits travel by its stroke and joint angle; a motor on the plate (FIG. 13, which the description attributes to US 4,976,582, Clavel) adds moving mass. Here the added actuator rides between the two parallel driven links of a leg, preferably next to the drive link, and drives a fixed-length shaft to a posture changing mechanism at the plate. One leg gives four axes; all three legs give six (FIG. 6). Further embodiments: a breakaway slip coupling in the shaft (FIG. 8) and a through hole for tubing (FIGS. 9, 10). Independent claims 1 and 5 also require the universal joint on the line between the two driven-link attachment points at the moving part.

glossary.def: Parallel robot with three rotary-driven upper arms, each joined to the platform by a parallelogram forearm, so the platform translates in three axes without tilting.
The patent's terms for the upper arm and the pair of forearm rods of a delta leg.
The patent's term (col 5) for a parallelogram.
In robotics, one independently driven degree of freedom.
The tool at the end of a robot, such as a gripper or suction pad.
Joint that transmits rotation between two shafts at an angle to each other.
Gear with teeth set at an angle to its axis; crossed pairs can connect non-parallel shafts.
Bar on a shaft and matching slot in a bore; they lock relative rotation and still allow axial sliding.
Multiple axial teeth on a shaft mating with matching grooves in a bore; a multi-key form of the same coupling.
The patent's term for a freely rotating connection that keeps tubing from winding up; the common name for such a fluid coupling is rotary union.
